---
title: "First the profit you want, then the price"
unit: 3
module: 1
duration: "10 min"
---

<Phase type="activation">

Remember how a retreat price is usually born. You open a few similar pages, see the numbers, and put yours somewhere in the middle. A little lower — so that people definitely buy.

**Now picture a builder who sets the price of a house by the plot next door, without opening the estimate.** Hold that picture for a few seconds.

</Phase>

<Phase type="reflection">

Go back to the builder with the estimate in their pocket. The house next door may have been smaller, simpler, or built at a loss.

**Someone else's price says nothing about your lines.** It only says that someone dared to name it.

</Phase>

<Phase type="concept">

## The reverse order

The honest order is this: first the profit you want from the retreat, then all the costs, and only then the price. Venues that have worked with leaders for a long time start the first conversation with exactly this question: "how much do you want to earn".

Profit is not greed. It is payment for your work, and that work has hours.

## How many hours are in one retreat

Preparing a retreat means the program, letters with the venue, sales, answering guests, logistics, the retreat itself and the review afterwards. Leaders name an order of a hundred hours or more for one week.

Work it out roughly: if honest profit is 22,200 dollars and the hours are 100, your hour is worth 222 dollars. If profit is 3,000, it is thirty. **Paying yourself is a separate line, not whatever "is left over".**

## The lines people forget

Besides the venue, the leader has their own costs. They are often remembered only on site:

- the leader's flight and transfer;
- a night on site before arrival, if you go early to set up the hall;
- phone and data on the trip, especially abroad;
- a photographer;
- gifts for guests;
- a transfer reserve for a guest who mixed up their flight time;
- excess baggage for equipment.

In the calculator such lines are added as fixed costs. Gifts go in as a cost per guest.

## The price from the profit

Take the [teaching deal](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#) and a target of 25,000 dollars of honest profit. Add the forgotten lines: flight 900, extra night 150, phone 120, photographer 1,500, transfer reserve 200 and gifts at 25 per guest.

Then the price comes out at about 3,320 dollars instead of 3,000. The formula is simple: profit plus the venue plus all the lines, divided by the guests, with an allowance for 3 % card fees.

**Prices are prices.** If the honest price is higher than the neighbours', that is not a calculation error. It is information: either the program has to be worth that money, or the model, the venue or the format changes.

<SelfCheck id="c3"/>

</Phase>

<Phase type="practice">

1. Open the [teaching deal](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#).
2. Add the fixed costs from the list above and a cost per guest — gifts.
3. See how far honest profit fell at a price of 3,000.
4. Raise the price in steps of 50 dollars until honest profit reaches 25,000. In the teaching deal that happens at 3,350.
5. Divide that profit by 100 hours and write down what your hour is worth.
6. Repeat for your own retreat: your target, your lines, your hours.

</Phase>
